task: Bounded TDD follow-up for durable journal namespace sync, hardlink refusal, and descriptor ownership cleanup

scope.environment: All project execution used nix develop and the existing project toolchain; no dependency changes or outside-Nix installs.

implementation: The fd-relative O_NOFOLLOW ancestor walk syncs each parent directory before releasing its descriptor. This includes parents of newly created directories and resyncs existing ancestors that may have been left by an earlier failed constructor.

After opening, validating, and locking the journal inode, construction fsyncs the private journal directory before returning. Append retains its existing flush plus journal-inode fsync before successful return. A directory-sync failure prevents construction and therefore prevents any note acknowledgement.

Regular journal validation now requires st_nlink == 1. Validation runs both during construction and again against the opened descriptor immediately before append's write. A link added after opening is rejected without writing and poisons the active writer.

Text conversion uses closefd=False so the store retains explicit raw-descriptor ownership even during partial text-wrapper initialization failure. Successful stores retain that raw descriptor until close, preserving the lifetime flock.

Constructor, ancestor-walk, and close cleanup attempt each owned descriptor independently while suppressing secondary syscall-close OSErrors. Originating exceptions remain unchanged. Close invalidates stored descriptor numbers before cleanup so repeated close does not close descriptors subsequently reused by another store.

tdd.method: Vertical RED then minimal GREEN slices; no production change preceded its corresponding failing test. Existing invariant checks added afterward are explicitly regression coverage, not novel RED claims.
tdd.command_prefix: nix develop -c uv run pytest tests/test_memory_journal_boundary.py

additional_existing_behavior_regressions: Constructor file-open failure closes all tracked descriptors and permits reopen.
Constructor file-validation failure closes all tracked descriptors and permits reopen.
Failure after a real flock acquisition closes the lock-owning descriptor and permits reopen.

Append-inode-sync failure preserves exception identity, poisons reads/appends, leaves bytes unchanged on blocked retry, retains the writer lock until explicit close, and releases both owned descriptors on close.

evidence_and_limits: Success-path syscall spies invoke the real mkdir and fsync on actual temporary filesystem directories and the journal inode, record their resolved descriptor targets, and assert namespace/data syncs precede append's successful return.

Failure-path injections operate on real open descriptors, real file wrappers, real hardlinks, and real flocks. Cleanup injections close the actual descriptor before reporting a secondary error. Tests check EBADF on all tracked descriptors and successful fresh writer acquisition afterward.

This exercises syscall ordering, fail-closed return behavior, exception identity, descriptor cleanup, and lock release on this Linux filesystem. It is not a power-loss simulation and does not establish physical power-loss tolerance, controller/cache behavior, or crash consistency on every filesystem.

No exactly-once retry guarantee is claimed. An append whose fsync fails can already have reached disk; a failed or lost acknowledgement can leave an uncertain outcome. A poisoned writer blocks automatic continuation; explicit inspection/repair/reopen remains necessary, and blindly retrying the same logical note may duplicate it.

The pre-append fstat detects an existing hardlink at that boundary, including links created after constructor success. It does not claim atomic protection against a malicious same-UID process linking the inode concurrently after validation.

All walked parents are synced at construction to cover failed-constructor leftovers. Startup latency was not benchmarked; unsupported or failed directory fsync remains fail-closed rather than being silently ignored.
